propositions: Jira Data Center and Cloud differ on three axes: REST API version (v2 vs v3), authentication (PAT bearer vs ACLI subprocess), and user identity (name vs accountId), preventing unified reconciliation without forking adapter code

Extracting shared Jira-family logic into a common seam prevents duplicate field maps and sanitizers from diverging, with both backends importing from the single definition rather than maintaining separate copies

Location-pinned modules (adf.py, outbound_fields.py, comment_limits.py) loaded by path cannot relocate without updating the dynamic loader, so sharing occurs via dependency inversion (pinned modules import from jira_family) rather than relocation

Behavioral variation between Cloud and DC is represented as pluggable contracts (RichTextCodec for ADF vs wiki-text, UserIdentityModel for accountId vs name) with one implementation per deployment, not forked code

TLS requirement and certificate verification cannot be disabled for DC connections, with an explicit allow_insecure override for test/private-network deployments that logs a warning rather than silencing the risk
The DC backend is gated behind a [jira-datacenter] optional extra and lazy-imported, keeping the core engine's dependency contract unchanged and the battle-tested Cloud path untouched
